claude_take: What jumps out across today's stories is how much energy institutions are spending to get faster, bigger, and more controlling: OpenAI slashing prices on its AI agents, Mistral throwing open a trillion-parameter model, Instagram chasing YouTube's turf with 90-minute videos, Louis Vuitton inserting a whole new executive layer above its own designers. Meanwhile the systems we already trusted kept failing in blunt, human ways: a signal fault in Spain let one train plow into another and kill dozens, and a losing Brazilian candidate treated a Supreme Court travel ban as a polite suggestion. The sharpest line for me is Jafar Panahi, a filmmaker the world just celebrated at Cannes, handed a new five-year sentence for the films that got him there. Everyone's selling speed and scale as progress today; accountability, somehow, isn't keeping up.

items.headline: OpenAI Launches GPT-6.1 Terra, Cutting Prices in Half for Faster AI Agents
items.summary: OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Terra on October 26, upgrading its mid-tier model with API pricing about 50 percent lower than its predecessors and more than triple the speed on computer-use tasks. The company says Terra approaches the performance of its flagship Astra model at a fraction of the cost, another step in the industry's push to make capable AI agents cheap enough for everyday, constant use.

items.headline: Mistral Releases Open Weights for Its Trillion-Parameter Large 4 Model
items.summary: Mistral has published open weights for Large 4, the trillion-parameter model it first opened for public preview earlier this month, letting developers download and run it themselves rather than access it only through Mistral's API. The French lab is positioning the release around strong agentic-coding and cyber-defense benchmarks, a notable bet on openness as US and Chinese rivals increasingly keep their largest models closed or gated.

items.headline: Iran Hands Cannes-Winning Director Jafar Panahi a New Five-Year Prison Sentence
items.summary: An Iranian Revolutionary Court sentenced filmmaker Jafar Panahi in absentia to five years and one month in prison, with asset confiscation and a travel ban, months after he won the Palme d'Or for "It Was Just an Accident" and returned to Iran despite a pending conviction. The new ruling stacks on top of an earlier one-year sentence and is a stark reminder of how little protection international acclaim offers directors working under Iran's government.

items.headline: Instagram Starts Testing 90-Minute Videos, Taking Direct Aim at YouTube
items.summary: Meta is rolling out a long-form horizontal video format on Instagram, called Features, that lets select creators upload videos up to 90 minutes long, alongside a tool for linking short Reels clips to the full video. The test began in Brazil and is expanding to a small group of US creators, with no revenue-sharing plan yet, marking Instagram's clearest move yet to pull long-form viewing away from YouTube rather than stay confined to short clips.

items.headline: At Least 64 Killed as Spanish High-Speed Train Slams Into Stopped Train Near Toledo
items.summary: A Renfe high-speed train struck the rear of a stationary Iryo train near Urda, in Toledo province, on October 28, derailing two coaches and killing at least 64 of the roughly 540 passengers involved, with authorities warning the toll could still rise. Spain's transport minister pointed to an electronic signaling failure near Urda station, making this the country's deadliest rail disaster since 2013 and its second major one this year.

items.headline: Flávio Bolsonaro Defies Court Order, Flees Brazil for Florida After Losing Runoff to Lula
items.summary: Days after losing Brazil's presidential runoff to Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro left the country for Florida by way of Argentina and Ecuador, defying a Supreme Court order to surrender his passports and stay put while facing money-laundering and tax-evasion investigations he denies. Lula called the move "shameful," saying Bolsonaro could have stayed and proven the accusations false, turning an already consequential election into a fresh test of whether Brazil's courts can actually enforce their own rulings.

items.headline: Louis Vuitton Creates New Chief Brand Creative Officer Role, Hires From Tiffany
items.summary: LVMH's flagship Louis Vuitton has created a new executive position and named Hector Muelas, formerly Tiffany & Co.'s global chief brand and creative officer, to lead brand storytelling and campaigns across all touchpoints starting November 1. He reports to deputy CEO Damien Bertrand rather than to the house's existing creative directors Pharrell Williams and Nicolas Ghesquière, formalizing marketing control as a function separate from design leadership.

items.headline: Marx's Alienation
items.summary: Karl Marx argued that under capitalism, workers become estranged from the product of their labor, from the act of working itself, from their own creative capacities, and from one another, because the things they make and the value they create end up belonging to someone else. The idea still shapes how critics describe modern work, from gig-economy platforms to AI tools that absorb a person's skill and judgment into a system they neither own nor control.
items.summary_fr: Pour Karl Marx, le travailleur sous le capitalisme devient étranger au produit de son travail, à l'acte même de travailler, à ses propres capacités créatrices, et aux autres travailleurs, puisque ce qu'il produit et la valeur qu'il crée finissent par appartenir à autrui. Cette idée éclaire encore aujourd'hui les critiques du travail contemporain, des plateformes de l'économie à la tâche jusqu'aux outils d'IA qui absorbent le savoir-faire d'une personne dans un système qu'elle ne possède ni ne maîtrise.
